jobs_results.description:
The Chan Zuckerberg Biohub San Francisco (CZ Biohub SF) is an independent nonprofit research institute that brings together Stanford, UC Berkeley, and UC San Francisco into a single collaborative technology and discovery engine. CZ Biohub SF supports bright, bold engineers, data scientists, and biomedical researchers to investigate the fundamental mechanisms underlying disease and develop new technologies that will lead to actionable diagnostics and effective therapies.

Our Vision

We pursue large scientific challenges that cannot be pursued in conventional environments.

We enable individual investigators to pursue their riskiest and most innovative ideas.

The technologies developed at CZ Biohub San Francisco facilitate research by scientists and clinicians at our home institutions and beyond.

The Opportunity
The Data Science platform at CZ Biohub SF is seeking an Associate Bioinformatics Scientist/Computational Biologist to join a team of computational biologists and data scientists. We develop computational methods, pipelines, and software that enable Biohub's research across quantitative cell biology and infectious disease. In this position, you will closely collaborate with biologists and engineers from research groups such as the Royer group and the Balla group.

Potential projects include

Developing workflows to process and analyze single‑cell multi‑omics datasets to gain a holistic view of transcriptional regulation during zebrafish development.

Participating in data integration across multiple modalities to create a resource for the broader scientific community.

Contributing to interactive web portals for in silico genetic perturbations on developing zebrafish at whole organism scale.

You will

Contribute to scientific discovery via analysis of single‑cell multi‑omics datasets (transcriptomic, epigenomic, and/or proteomic).

Participate in developing bioinformatics tools and web portals.

Optimize and execute data processing pipelines in an HPC environment.

Partner with biologists to conduct data mining and exploratory data analysis.

Author publications and disseminate research discoveries to the scientific community.

You have

S. or M.S. degree in Data Science, Computational Biology, Bioinformatics, or a related discipline.

A minimum of 2 years of experience with scientific programming languages and data science workflows (e.g., Python, R, Git, UNIX command line).

Familiarity with professional software development best practices (documentation, version control).

Proven ability to implement exploratory data analysis and statistical inference in scientific research.

A collaborative, team‑focused mindset coupled with outstanding communication skills and the ability to work in an agile environment.

Nice to have

Experience with single‑cell RNA‑seq data analysis and/or other multi‑dimensional omic data modalities.

Familiarity with concepts of molecular biology, cell biology, genomics, and biostatistics.

Experience with high‑performance computing clusters and job schedulers such as Slurm.

Enthusiasm for systems biology and development of open‑source software.

Experience with machine learning algorithms to extract insights from complex datasets.

Research experience in academic laboratories is highly preferred.

Compensation

$72,000-$99,000

What We Provide

Resources to disrupt and innovate at the frontiers of biology and disease.

A collegial and collaborative environment of diverse expertise.

Existing collaborations within CZ Biohub across technology platforms and research group leaders.

Access to collaborators, resources, and facilities at partner universities and organizations.

Competitive compensation and benefits commensurate with experience.

Benefits
We offer a robust benefits program that includes healthcare coverage, life and disability insurance, commuter subsidies, family planning services, childcare stipend, 401(k) match, flexible time off, and a generous parental leave policy. We also honor our commitment to career development through regular onsite opportunities to learn from leading scientists.

We do not discriminate based on age, race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, disability, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or any other protected status in accordance with applicable law.

jobs_results.title: Bioinformatics AI Expert - Advanced Benchmark Data Annotator

job_highlights.title: Qualifications
items: Data Workspace Packaging: Build clean, self-contained zip workspace archives containing real or synthesized biological datasets (e.g., expression tables, sequence files, metadata)

job_highlights.title: Responsibilities
items: In this role, you will design complex, reasoning-intensive, "information-reversal" evaluation tasks to measure the autonomous tool-use and data analysis capabilities of Agent-style Large Language Models (LLMs) on real "wet lab / dry lab" biological data (e.g., RNA-seq, FASTQ, BAM, mzML)

Key Responsibilities Information-Reversal Problem Creation: Construct complex scientific scenario questions where AI models receive anonymized raw/processed biological datasets and must deduce hidden identities, experimental conditions, variant locations, or functional pathways

Multi-Step Tool Orchestration: Design tasks that strictly require multi-step external tool execution (e.g., BLAST, genomic interval tools, variant annotators, phylogenetic software, differential expression pipelines) rather than simple code execution or direct text lookups

Chain of Thought (CoT) & Rubric Engineering: Author step-by-step resolution paths and rigid all-or-nothing grading rubrics featuring canonical answers and explicitly accepted variants for automated LLM evaluation

Quality Assurance & Verification: Ensure all benchmark deliverables pass automated validation checks, eliminating answer leakage in metadata or filenames, and guaranteeing single, deterministic correct answers

jobs_results.job_title: Bioinformatics AI Expert - Advanced Benchmark Data Annotator

Key Responsibilities Information-Reversal Problem Creation: Construct complex scientific scenario questions where AI models receive anonymized raw/processed biological datasets and must deduce hidden identities, experimental conditions, variant locations, or functional pathways.


Data Workspace Packaging: Build clean, self-contained zip workspace archives containing real or synthesized biological datasets (e.g., expression tables, sequence files, metadata). Multi-Step Tool Orchestration: Design tasks that strictly require multi-step external tool execution (e.g., BLAST, genomic interval tools, variant annotators, phylogenetic software, differential expression pipelines) rather than simple code execution or direct text lookups. Chain of Thought (CoT) & Rubric Engineering: Author step-by-step resolution paths and rigid all-or-nothing grading rubrics featuring canonical answers and explicitly accepted variants for automated LLM evaluation.


Quality Assurance & Verification: Ensure all benchmark deliverables pass automated validation checks, eliminating answer leakage in metadata or filenames, and guaranteeing single, deterministic correct answers.

jobs_results.description:
Senior Bioinformatics Scientist Specializing In Ai-Enabled Protein Design And Engineering
What if the work you did every day could impact the lives of people you know? Or all of humanity? At Illumina, we are expanding access to genomic technology to realize health equity for billions of people around the world. Our efforts enable life-changing discoveries that are transforming human health through the early detection and diagnosis of diseases and new treatment options for patients. Working at Illumina means being part of something bigger than yourself. Every person, in every role, has the opportunity to make a difference. Surrounded by extraordinary people, inspiring leaders, and world changing projects, you will do more and become more than you ever thought possible.


We are seeking a Senior Bioinformatics Scientist specializing in AI-enabled protein design and engineering to help invent the next generation of enzyme reagents that power Illumina sequencing platforms. Working at the intersection of machine learning, structural biology, and protein engineering, you will apply state-of-the-art computational approaches to design enzymes that expand the performance and capabilities of Illumina technologies. The role is based in San Diego. This is an exciting opportunity to be a part of Illumina's continued growth.


Responsibilities:



Develop and apply tailored bioinformatics tools and pipelines to design, engineer, and/or discover novel enzymes.
Apply modern AI approaches, including protein language models, generative design methods, and structure-based machine learning, to predict and optimize enzyme function.
Evaluate application, development, and implementation of novel computational methods and AI technologies to leverage protein sequence, structure, and/or experimental data for enzyme engineering.
Create reusable templates, scripts, dashboards, or lightweight applications that allow project teams to run routine analyses and review computational recommendations more efficiently.
Contribute to standards for data capture, model evaluation, design rationale, and reproducible computational workflows.
Analyze high-throughput screening and sequencing datasets to guide protein optimization.
Participate in multi-disciplinarily protein engineering projects and interact with engineers, chemists, biophysicists, and protein scientists, to deliver protein variants with desired properties.

Requirements:



Typically requires a minimum of 5 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree; or 3 years and a Master's degree; or a PhD without experience; or equivalent work experience.
Practical experience developing and applying AI/ML methods to protein and enzyme engineering
Solid programming skills in at least one of the major programming languages (e.g., C/C++, Python, R).
In-depth knowledge of protein sequence or structure modelling, protein-ligand interaction predictions and/or molecular simulations.
Strong fundamentals in statistical modelling, algorithm design, data analysis, and/or visualization methods.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Collaborative, open and self-aware, team player, and able to rapidly integrate into cross functional teams.
Highly motivated individual with proven ability in thinking innovatively and the proven track record of productive research and development.

The estimated base salary range for the Senior Bioinformatics Scientist – AI/ML for Protein Engineering role based in the United States of America is: $129,400 – $194,000. Should the level or location of the role change during the hiring process, the applicable base pay range may be updated accordingly. The range reflects long‑term growth in the role; therefore, most candidates are hired between the minimum and middle of the range. Placement depends on experience, skills, location, and internal equity. Additionally, all employees are eligible for one of our variable cash programs (bonus or commission) and eligible roles may receive equity as part of the compensation package. We offer a wide range of benefits as innovative as our work, including access to genomics sequencing, family planning, health/dental/vision, retirement benefits, and paid time off.
